method: Actual PNG contact-sheet inspection of all scheduled endpoint, intermediate and held-pose images. Prior revisions of these four seed slots were familiar, so this rerun review is independent but not fully blinded. Case mapping was used for diagnosis after inspecting the005 images.

scoreAnchors.1: minor variant or substantial readability/continuity defect
scoreAnchors.2: clear evolved form or coherent readable development

scoringNotes: Endpoint/pose distinctiveness refers to the previous milestone. Intermediate distinctiveness refers to the interval's initial form and can correctly be1 early in a continuous transition. Exact birth is expected to score0 for distinctiveness. All frames receive their own explicit record; pose coherence evaluates the complete ordered eight-phase group rather than a single frozen image.

clearEvolution.condition: All adjacent milestone comparisons scored at least2 for perceived distinctiveness

continuityAtLeast2.condition: All adjacent milestone comparisons scored at least2 for temporal continuity

gateConclusion: The small proof005 visual cohort passes clear-evolution and continuity gates. This is not a whole-product release approval or a claim that all genotypes are unique.

defects.issue: Thin connective growth stalks are now connected but temporarily dominate the silhouette before upper/lower segment masses fill out.
Both elder endpoints approach a long-tailed raised-face body plan. Their proportions differ but body-plan family convergence should remain visible in later diversity results.
Walking motion is concentrated in small lower support pixels beneath a large stacked body; the held poses differ but locomotion is less immediately legible than the quadruped.

limitations: Only one starting infant and four fixed neutral-care seeds are represented.
Contact sheets and ordered complete pose groups were inspected, not physical-device playback.
A separate hollow-white-head contrast defect identified during review was subsequently fixed and its focused regression passes; it was not a bean-cohort visual finding.
No cross-preset population diversity or genetic/care variance conclusion follows from this small proof.

comparisons.notes: A separate small head and neck develop above a disproportionately larger lower mass; this is recognizable reorganization beyond uniform enlargement.
Upright bulb becomes a horizontal articulated quadruped with redistributed head, trunk, tail and support. Knees and alternating support are visible.

Horizontal quadruped becomes an upright segmented stack with a different mass arrangement and support. At days90/97.5/105 new segment masses grow through thin material bridges; these are now connected, though the temporary stalks are visually awkward.
Compact infant becomes a tall narrow body with head above it and a two-foot stance.
Tall support form broadens into a deep round body with a prominent upper face while support anatomy is absorbed.
Filled round body opens into a hollow ring with the face preserved on a material crown. The negative-space change is substantial and readable.
Round infant becomes a broad four-legged body with separate head and neck.
Quadruped becomes a low sloping aquatic body with reduced support and a more prominent forward face. Changes are clear but less extreme than this cohort's other transitions.
Low aquatic body becomes an elongated tapering serpentine form with raised face and wave-driven motion.

Borderline but passes2: the infant becomes a flattened armored profile with a distinct back/shoulder contour, seam and forward facial region. Proportion redistribution plus surface organization make it more than enlargement alone.
Horizontal armored profile becomes a very tall limbless column with raised face, reversing its mass arrangement and support presentation.
Tall column becomes a low long-tailed body with a raised face. Its endpoint approaches seed3's broad form family, which is a diversity weakness rather than failure of this adjacent transition.
